The new implementation is backwards compatible, interface-wise, yet it is still not usable for wrapping arbitrary repositories and providing a _working_ `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository` implementation.

Typically, when a type extends/implements an interface, it does so not only in contract, but by actually fulfilling the interface's described and expected behavior. When an interface supports optional components, it can define methods which state the level of support (e.g. `isDataSourceAware`, `canWrite`, etc.). Alternatively, when it is not possible to implement the whole of an interface, an exception is thrown from the unsupported methods.

In my initial [comment about the backward compatibility issue](https://github.com/pentaho/pentaho-platform/pull/5124#discussion_r956185252), I proposed the following solution which I think would not suffer from this problem:

> If we'd be given a `IMetadataDomainRepository` which is not a `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository`, we could create a wrapper that would implement the extra functionality, instead of backing it all in the implementation of `PentahoMetadataDomainRepository`.

However, being able to always provide the extra functionality of `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository`, given any `IMetadataDomainRepository`, while possible, will not be as efficient because the data source type would need to be discovered everytime, using the old, slow method (by calling `getDomain(.)` and parsing the domain file). Any efficient implementation relies on access to the underlying data store (typically the JCR repository) to store the data source type as a metadata attribute of the domain file. Concluding, with this solution, the slow and fast implementations would both need to exist and be maintained separately.

Another solution would be to subclass `SessionCachingMetadataDomainRepository` and define a new `DataSourceTypeAwareSessionCachingMetadataDomainRepository` class which would implement `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository` and would require being given a `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository` delegate. The original class would be mostly unchanged. The new class would be used in Pentaho code, while any third-parties could safely continue using the old class.

Another solution would be to change the current implementation (of this commit) to throw """"not supported"""" when `getMetadataDomainIds` or `getDataSourceWizardDomainIds` where called and `delegate` were not an `IDataSourceAwareMetadataDomainRepository`. This would preserve the """"conditional"""" nature of the implementation, while avoiding improper use.

We could conclude that these changes inevitably represent/require a breaking change and then go back to incorporating the """"data source type"""" of a metadata domain in the `IMetadataDomainRepository` interface, by adding a method such as: `@NonNull String getDataSourceType( String domainId )`.

The data source type would remain _open_, at this place — actual data source types could be defined elsewhere (in the pentaho platform project). Alternatively, if we find that we could _close_ the data source types here, we could return an enumeration, instead of a `String`, and even provide methods which returned the subset of domain ids for each of the data source types (as is currently proposed).

In any case, based on this new method, one could easily filter the result of `getDomainIds()` to those of any desired data source type. This method would allow for an efficient implementation (by handling the file metadata attributes upgrade on the fly, whenever the data source type file metadata attribute was not present).

While this would be a breaking change, it would at least simplify the problem immensely, by stopping the possibility of there existing metadata domain repositories not """"exported"""" by some _data source_ on its tracks. It is this possibility that raises the difficulties downstream to propagate the extra information, conditionally and efficiently.

While, as is, the `IMetadataDomainRepository` is more abstract, I believe/suspect it is never practically used in its current form, i.e. without its data source being considered downstream — need to check this is the case, at least in Pentaho maintained code!
